source_evidence: it might only be able to buy half a loaf
answer: Inflation can reduce the purchasing power of savings: even if your account balance grows by earning interest, the money may buy less if prices rise faster. For example, the source describes a dollar that once bought a loaf of bread but, years later, might buy only half a loaf even with interest added. This is why the amount of money you have and what that money can buy are not always the same.
